highlights.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come true
highlights.summary: Nintendo Switch 2; Nintendo This ambitious remake transforms Zelda into a modern masterpiece, clearer and easier to navigate, more beautiful to look at, with playful musical touches, yet the melancholy remains. It’s always a worry, returning to a formative piece of art from your childhood.
body: Light-touch remasters aim to bring such games up to modern graphical standards without fundamentally changing them; an ambitious remake attempts to transform the work into something that can stand alongside any modern masterpiece. Ocarina of Time is the latter. And I could not be more delighted to report that it is a dream come true.

What has changed is how all of this is framed. Ocarina of Time’s story was once told through necessary understatement: you could not fit reams of dialogue and hours of cinematics onto a Nintendo 64 cartridge in 1998. Text chatter with Hyrule’s denizens has been spruced up and expanded here, so that the world feels more alive: it’s funnier and more colourful. But more importantly, pivotal moments in this story play out in fully voiced cutscenes (don’t worry, Link himself remains silent) that recall 2023’s Tears of the Kingdom.

highlights.title: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
highlights.summary: The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare "whether AI has been used in their work," the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform.
body: Nexus Mods says that authors of newly uploaded mods will have to declare whether AI was ‘used in their work.’

“One of the most consistent concerns we’ve heard is that it’s not clearly disclosed when AI has been used to create a mod,” according to the post from site owner Victor “Foledinho” Folmann. “We already have tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods, but we recognise that there’s a lot more we can do to make that information more accessible and clear for you all.” Any mods tagged as “AI-assisted” will also be required to include “a public explanation of how and where AI was used.” AI tags will also be “more prominent” on mod pages.

The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable. An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use. We’d prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform.

highlights.title: Netflix's Assassin's Creed Live-Action Series Officially Wraps Up Filming
highlights.summary: Netflix unveiled its plans to make a live-action Assassin's Creed series in 2020. Development only began in 2025 when Halo 's screenwriter David Wiener and Roberto Patino came on board. Six years after the announcement of this project, as reported by Matt's Inside Line, filming is complete.
body: Netflix's live-action series isn't the first attempt to take the Assassin's Creed franchise beyond the world of video games. In 2016, Michael Fassbender entered the Animus as Cal Lynch to access the memories of his ancestor Aguilar de Nerha, a 15th-century assassin from Spain. Unfortunately, the movie was not well-received, scoring a mere 18% on Rotten Tomatoes.

Assassin's Creed fans have traveled all over the world as different members of the Assassin Brotherhood. Netflix will take them back to Rome in its upcoming live-action series, the city where Ezio Auditore fought the Borgia family in the early 16th century in Assassin's Creed: Brotherhood. However, they won't come across one of the series' most beloved characters, as the show will take place in 64 AD, a long time before Ezio Auditore.

Instead, they will find themselves in an ancient Rome ruled by Emperor Nero. According to Netflix, its focal point will be the secret war between two "shadowy factions," — presumably the Templar Order and the Assassin Brotherhood — played out across "pivotal historical events." Beyond that, not much is known about the plot; more is likely to be revealed soon.

highlights.summary: Pups that carry your shopping are one thing – but what about the mechanical canines being bought up in the US by ICE? Or the mutant mutts due to be developed by a startup called Warhound? Have you ever wanted to hang out with a dog with no fur, no face and a chip in its shoulder?
body: What exactly will these machines do when they can act more independently? The founder of Dimensional insists they will help people. They might carry groceries home, for example, which is certainly something my tiny chihuahua-mix is incapable of.

While it is nice to think that robo dogs are all going to be very good boys, there is a darker side to the industry. A couple of months ago it was reported that US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) planned to spend up to $2m (£1.5m) on robot dogs made by the company Boston Dynamics. ICE has said the dogs won’t be used for anything nefarious but, considering everything the agency has been up to lately, this isn’t particularly reassuring.

highlights.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time never gets old
highlights.summary: Breath of the Wild changed everything. Two decades after The Legend of Zelda made the transformational shift to 3D, Breath of the Wild reinvigorated the franchise with an open-ended adventure that was built around player freedom and expression.
body: The franchise has evolved since 1998, but the first 3D Zelda stands up incredibly well in its Switch 2 remake.

The story remains unchanged from the original. It’s a third-person action-adventure game where you play as a little forest dweller named Link who gets pulled into an adventure to save the fantasy realm of Hyrule from a villain named Ganondorf. That’s true of basically every Zelda title, and here the twist comes from a musical instrument (the titular flute-like ocarina) imbued with magical powers. Over the course of the game you learn songs that can change the weather, warp you across the landscape, mess with the flow of time, and more.

The original Ocarina was renowned both for its large 3D world and for the intricacy of its dungeons, which required using the ocarina, along with various other items, to solve puzzles in clever ways. At a certain point you’re even jumping back and forth in time, navigating spaces as both tiny Link and his adult version. The challenge steadily grows in complexity right up until you face Ganondorf in his castle, forcing you to use a huge range of items at your disposal.

highlights.title: Please stop asking me when the AI bubble will pop
highlights.summary: People, including on this staff, keep asking me with varying degrees of excitement or trepidation when the AI bubble will burst. I'll tell you what I tell them: If I knew that, I would make a life-changing bet on the market, levered up as far as I could, and then, after I made my money, go retire…
body: What I can tell you is that I read with interest a story in Bloomberg this morning: “ Wall Street CEOs, Big Money Managers Divided Over AI Risks.” The story itself is a roundup of stuff said at the 2026 Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit in Hong Kong. Here’s what caught my attention: The CEO of Pacific Investment Management Co. — that’s PIMCO, the legendary bond firm — told listeners that there’s going to be a downturn in the AI market “and then things are going to break.”

The astronomically expensive AI buildout has swamped debt markets — making it harder to raise cash. But there’s still more debt coming, and people still want to buy it. For instance, Meta drew $58 billion in orders for a bond offering that’s expected to be $15 billion to $20 billion, Bloomberg reported today. Oracle said Monday it would need another $20 billion in bonds, on top of its existing steep commitments. Alphabet, Google’s parent company, is selling €6 billion (or about $6.7 billion) of bonds. Even Microsoft recently sold bonds, for the first time in a decade — $25 billion of them.

highlights.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Still Perfect on Switch 2 | Review
highlights.summary: As the time-afflicted Link comes to learn in the seminal Nintendo 64 classic, a lot can change in seven years. Shifting political struggles leave a neighborhood in total disrepair. That one local eccentric he came to love is nowhere to be seen.
body: Somewhere among all its gods and ghosts, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time draws its true power from its human center: a familiar story about growing up and returning home after a long absence.

It’s what makes the concept of an Ocarina of Time remake so challenging, but impossible to resist. How fitting — fated even, written in stars and ancient code — to bring generations of adventurers back to the sprawling field where they first learned to run. Like your hometown, a game as foundational as this is perhaps meant to be revisited throughout a lifetime rather than locked away in your long-term memory.

Nintendo doesn’t squander the opportunity for a meaningful homecoming in its lovingly crafted Switch 2 remake. The timeless classic is still a joy to reappraise in its dazzling new form, even if some of its modern developments might send protective fans marching to town hall. Yes, there’s a Starbucks where that quaint café used to be now, but Ocarina of Time ’s soul still shines bright enough to guide you home.

highlights.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: eye creams that are worth using down to the last drop
highlights.summary: Face cream is often enough, but if you want a separate product for your eyes, these new ones are terrific value. A hill I will die on: you do not necessarily need an eye cream. There are, I will admit, reasons why you might fare better with one.
body: It may, of course, be none of the above, but just that you find using an eye cream a pleasure, which is as good a reason as any.

My point is that eye creams are not the anti-ageing magic bullet that marketing campaigns would have us believe. Very many of us can do the same job with our facial skincare, saving time and cash. But if you would still like to try one without the considerable financial commitment that many require, there are some new eye creams that represent terrific value for money.

The Inkey List has a number of eye creams at great prices that cleverly address most of the variables above. Its latest offering, Bio-Active Ceramide Eye Cream (£15), is ideal for someone who prefers a fresh, watery day cream but craves a little richness around the eyes. It provides lasting, creamy, expensive-feeling hydration without feeling greasy, and it absorbs quickly. A peptide complex may support an improvement in firmness long-term (the company says a three-month blind clinical trial yielded positive results).

highlights.title: Building connections across the research infrastructure
highlights.summary: MIT.nano and the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition gathered facility leaders and technology professionals from across the nation to explore ways to make shared-access facilities more connected.
body: Running a modern research laboratory requires more than maintaining sophisticated instruments. Researchers need to complete training, obtain access, schedule and operate equipment, navigate billing, and more. For large, shared facilities, coordinating these activities across hundreds of instruments and thousands of users can be a significant undertaking. As research becomes increasingly interdisciplinary, another challenge is emerging: finding the right capability in the first place.

Addressing these challenges was a central theme of the 2026 NEMO User Meeting, hosted by MIT.nano Oct. 5–6. The meeting brought together 65 representatives from 25 laboratories and organizations, including facility directors, laboratory managers, technical staff, software developers, industry representatives, and government researchers. Sponsored by the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition ( NEMC ) hub, the meeting focused on sharing approaches to lab management and building connections among facilities.

highlights.title: How Long Is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake?
highlights.summary: You may well think you know the answer if you’re one of the many millions who hold Link’s first 3D adventure close to their hearts. But the remake is here almost 30 years later, and things have changed a little.
body: So, just how much time should you put aside to finish the Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake, and can you squeeze it in before GTA 6 arrives? We have three different accounts for you to read through, which detail just how many hours it took, and how that time was spent.

I’ve spent 45 hours with Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, across two separate save files. Before I get into my time spent, I will point out that Ocarina of Time only supports one save file! It kind of gives the impression that it supports multiple – when you start a new game, it only warns you that the five autosave points will be overwritten – but manually saving on your new file will overwrite your original file. I almost lost my 100% file this way, but luckily grabbed it from the cloud save.

highlights.title: ‘Every family has silences’: Kathryn Hunter on despair, desire, dislodgeable limbs – and her acting genius
highlights.summary: She has played King Lear, all three witches in Macbeth and an ape turned variety performer in Kafka’s Monkey. As she prepares for a new show, she discusses the soaring highs and deep lows of her extraordinary life. Kathryn Hunter pulls off her black beanie and sits down.
body: She is working on a stage adaptation of Eurotrash, Christian Kracht’s novel about a mother, played by Hunter, who is accompanied on the final trip of her life by her son, played by Ben Whishaw. As the pair come to terms with their dark past – and Europe’s – they must confront what Hunter describes as a “hinterland of silence”. In this case, it stems from the family’s Nazi ties, but Hunter believes “people will relate to it … in that every family has silences”. Working on the play has got her thinking about her own mother – and about the actor Marcello Magni, the co-founder of Complicité theatre and the love of Hunter’s life, who died in 2022 at 63.

Four years ago, Hunter ended her own long silence by clarifying that the life-changing injuries she suffered at 23 were not the result of a car accident, as was widely reported, but a suicide attempt. It was a sort of “coming out”, she says: “To come clean and make the plea for people in trouble to reach out and break silence … and rediscover the miracle that life can be.” She wants others to know that suicidal feelings “can be healed and it’s not something to be ashamed of; anyone can fall through the loop”.

highlights.title: New Jersey’s New Ebike Law Is Causing Chaos
highlights.summary: Since early 2026, the law has required electric bike owners to get licenses—and in some cases, insurance—to ride. It has left many stranded and confused.
body: In January, outgoing New Jersey governor Pat Murphy signed a first-in-the-nation bill that sought to make roads safer for everyone.

S-4834, passed by a wide bipartisan margin and sponsored by state Senate president Nick Scutari, was motivated by the “dramatic increase” in ebike use, which “created greater dangers for their operators, other motorists, and pedestrians,” Scutari wrote in a statement. Several teenagers in his district and elsewhere in the state had died on two-wheeled motorized vehicles, including a 13-year-old boy who died last fall after colliding with a landscaping truck.

The new law requires anyone who owns and rides a bike with pedal-assist tech or a throttle to be at least 15 years old and to have a license, either a driver’s license or a motorized bicycle license. (Riders can receive a stand-alone motorized bicycle only after passing a road test.) Riders must register their ebikes with the state’s Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC), and anyone on a bike that can travel faster than 20 mph must have insurance.

highlights.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) review
highlights.summary: I have a friend who first played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time back in the day, when the game was only just released and he was home from university for Christmas.
body: Here's what he meant. He'd play all day, curtains drawn, family ignored, working through dungeons and pelting across Hyrule Field on Epona. Then in the evening he'd call his girlfriend, who was back with her own family for Christmas. She always wanted to know what he'd got up to that day. And not in East Sussex; she wanted to know what he'd got up to in Hyrule.

So as he played he took regular breaks to tell someone else about what he had encountered, and what he had discovered, and what he had yet to overcome. It is my bright delight today to be able to tell you that, around thirty years later, having just revisited the game in Nintendo's new remake, Ocarina of Time is still worth telling people about. It's still an adventure so surprising, so satisfying, so moving that I need to talk about it.

highlights.title: What’s the Difference Between an Ebike and an E-Moto?
highlights.summary: Riders and lawmakers often don’t know the difference, and retailers sometimes muddy the waters on purpose. Here’s how to buy the micromobility vehicle you actually want.
body: The good: US sales are way up from the start of the decade, after the pandemic sparked interest in two-wheelers and helped riders go farther, faster, and with less effort. More people also see ebikes as viable transportation options and as more affordable and accessible alternatives to increasingly expensive cars. The bad? Sales are down from two years ago, and bike manufacturers and sellers have suffered. Riding injuries are up, notably among children, and lawmakers are looking for ways to control them.

Part of the issue is that people struggle to understand the difference between types of ebikes, and between ebikes and their faster cousins, e-motos. This often isn’t their fault. Lawmakers and vehicle retailers themselves have blurred the edges of the product categories, even though many places require riders of the most powerful ebikes and e-motos to meet age, licensing, and registration requirements.

highlights.title: Nexus Mods Forces Mandatory AI Disclosures and Filters, Explains Why It Won't Ban AI Mods
highlights.summary: Generative AI has taken over the modding scene, with modders mashing together existing games and using AI-assisted code to, for example, put the Nemesis system from Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor into Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2.
body: Nexus Mods, the biggest platform for mods on the internet, has reacted by enforcing mandatory disclosure for mods with AI-assisted code, and letting users filter AI-assisted mods out of their search criteria or preferences.
"We are pro-human creativity," Nexus Mods co-owner Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann said in a blog post, before further explaining why the site won’t outright ban AI mods entirely.

“You may ask me why [we won’t ban AI mods], since that is not the solution some of you were looking for,” he said. “The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable."

Foledinho believes an outright ban would just encourage modders to hide AI use. “It should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform," he said.

highlights.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
highlights.summary: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
body: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.
Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.

Anthropic is working on an open source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system, called FlashProve, is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” — a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using.

Similar to cryptographic email signatures that let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results.

highlights.summary: ArenaNet may be hard at work on a new entry in the Guild Wars series, but it apparently won't stop it from releasing brand-new content for the 21-year-old original. Guild Wars Afterlife has just been announced, and it's a full paid expansion for Guild Wars arriving next January.
body: Excitingly for old-school Guild Wars fans, Afterlife seems to bring back some content from the long-cancelled Utopia campaign, including the mystical, Mesoamerican-inspired setting of Xotecha. The new expansion will take players away from the continent of Tyria and into the Mists to explore the lost land of the dead.

The expansion's mechanics seem to be purpose-built for replayability. Xotecha's new dungeon is an ever-changing expanse called the Unformed, where no two runs will be the same. This dynamic design even extends to your character build, with a custom skill-drafting mechanic allowing you to change up your abilities on the fly.
While the skill-drafting mechanic seems unique to Xotecha, playing through Afterlife lets players unlock rewards they can take back with them out of the Mists.

Afterlife will be the second true expansion for the original Guild Wars, after 2007's Eye of the North. Players looking to get into the new expansion will need Guild Wars Reforged, the 2025 re-release of the original game.
